saints.name: St. Joan of Arc
saints.title: Virgin
saints.shortBlurb: The peasant girl who, led by heavenly voices, lifted the siege of Orléans and died at the stake at nineteen…
biography: Born about 1412 at Domrémy on the borders of Lorraine, the daughter of peasants, Joan never learned to read or write. From the age of thirteen she heard the voices of Sts. Michael, Catherine, and Margaret, who bade her go to the aid of the dauphin Charles and drive the English from France.

In 1429, after winning over the captain at Vaucouleurs and then the dauphin himself at Chinon, she led a relief army into besieged Orléans; the English raised the siege nine days after her arrival. The victory at Patay opened the road to Reims, where Charles VII was crowned in July 1429 with Joan standing by the altar.

Captured by the Burgundians at Compiègne in May 1430 and sold to the English, she was tried for heresy at Rouen under Pierre Cauchon, Bishop of Beauvais, and burned in the marketplace on 30 May 1431, about nineteen years old. A retrial quashed the sentence in 1456. Canonized in 1920 by Pope Benedict XV, the maiden-soldier who kept faith to the pyre is a patron of France and of soldiers.
saints.knownFor: The Maid of Orléans who freed France and died at the stake.

sources.text: Butler, Lives of the Saints (1866 ed.), 30 May
